newsitem.title: USA: Troubled Maine Yankee nuke plant names manager.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Maine Yankee nuke plant names manager.

text.p: A veteran Entergy Corp plant manager, Michael Sellman, will become chief nuclear officer of the trouble Maine Yankee nuclear plant, the two companies announced Friday.

Sellman's appointment comes just over two weeks after Maine Yankee signed a memorandum of understanding for Entergy -- a New Orleans-based utility holding company -- to provide management services at the Wiscasset, Maine facility.
Sellman is vice president for operations of Entergy's Waterford 3 nuclear unit, which like Maine Yankee was criticized last year by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission for equipment repair problems.

Entergy and Maine Yankee officials praised Sellman, who has also been general manager of Arkansas Nuclear One and River Bend plants, as having a track record of improving nuclear facilities that had suffered operational problems.

"His experience at other nuclear facilities will help set the course for regulatory and operational excellence at Maine Yankee," David Flanagan, president of Central Maine Power Co said in a statement.

The NRC is considering if the management agreement between Maine Yankee and Entergy will require a modification of Maine Yankee's operating license. Liability for violations is among the concerns, an official said.

Sellman will replace Charles Frizzle who was forced out as Maine Yankee's president in December. The plant's directors said at the time Maine Yankee needed to regain the trust of the public and regulators.
Sellman's appointment is subject to approval by Maine Yankee's board. He is expected to assume his duties in Maine in February, officials said.

Anti-nuclear activists have launched a referendum drive to force Maine Yankee's shutdown. Four previous efforts have failed, but this campaign's organizors say the plant's problems has generated public safety concern.

Maine Yankee has been shut down repeatedly in the past two years for problems ranging from steampipe leaks to improperly removed electrical cables. It has been off-line since Dec. 6 and is currently inspecting for leaking fuel rods.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, five percent by Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
